_note: FROSTMERE, OUTSIDE. The storm variants are gated on act4_done, the same flag data/dialogue/common.json uses for every other settlement -- see the _storm note in that file. Frostmere is the one town where the pre-storm lines could not simply be left alone underneath, because this town MEASURES the weather for a living and would have noticed first: so the base tier already has people who are uneasy, and the act4_done tier is them stopping being polite about it. Nobody here blames Meridian. They blame the lake, and they are wrong, and that is the point.

lines: In today: nine. Out today: eleven. You can see the problem with that.
Two of them are Foundation and they went up the trail, so I have stopped counting them.
I do not like having a column I have stopped counting.
You are in the book now. Name, hour, and which way you came.
You go out, you tell me. You do not go out, you tell me that too.
Nobody here thinks that is rude. Down your way I gather they do.
I have trimmed every lamp on this street twice this week and I will do it again tonight.
The wind is coming down the pass in a way it does in March. It is not March.
So the ropes go up early and I do not care how it looks.
Blue burns cold and burns slow and it is the one light nobody's window makes.
That is all it is. There is no charm in it and no mystery in it.
A stranger walks at a warm light and finds a wall. We had that happen once.
You went down and came back up and Eira let you have it. Good.
She would not have, if you had gone across it the way people do the first time.
The Hall takes challengers in the order they put their name at the desk.
I am not a challenger. I am here because our chimney is out and the Hall is warm.
You go on ahead. Genuinely. That is what the room is for.
Dad says we are not to go on the lake. Not the middle bit, ANY of it.
He has never said any of it before. He says the middle bit every year.
I can hold the rope from our door to the Hall with my eyes shut. I have done it.
Mum timed me. It is eleven and a bit if you do not stop at the fire.
Four households on nothing and it is not the middle of the season yet.
They are all ice families. No cut, no wage, no fuel. It runs downhill like that.
They are in the inn and they will stay in the inn. That part still works.
Every stack in this town is measured and the figure goes on the board in the inn.
Not to shame anybody. So that we know who to walk a barrow to before they ask.
Asking is the hard part. We took it out of the arrangement two hundred years ago.
Twelve inches is a floor. Five is a lid. I have five, and I have had five for eleven days.
Rain. In this valley, at this height, in the deep of the year. Twice.
I have no column in my book for rain. I have had to rule one.
Frostmere sells winter. That is the whole of it, and it is not a joke.
Sawn, stacked in straw, and it goes south to eleven towns that have no other cold.
Two hundred years we have done it and the lake has never once been late.
Saw is oiled. Sled is greased. Team is fed. Ice is five inches.
So I stand here, and I look at it, and at noon I go and look at it again.
Do not come past the last stack. I am not being unfriendly.
You can see where it goes from white to a sort of grey-white. That is the line.
Everything past it is a picture of a floor.
Something came in off the mountain last night and went along the shore in the dark.
Four of them. Big. Not ours -- ours would not come down to the water.
They were going somewhere and they did not stop, and that is what I did not like.
Somebody has to be looking at it. That is not superstition, that is the rota.
You watch a lake and you know its noises. When it takes, it grumbles all night.
It has not grumbled once. It has been quiet since the middle of last month.
Runners want greasing whether or not there is anything to put on them.
You let a sledge stand a season and the wood forgets what it is for. So do people.
Four hours up, and I would not, not this week, not for anybody.
There is weather sitting on the shoulder that has not moved in nine days.
Weather moves. That is the one thing about it you can rely on and it is not doing it.
The trail goes up to the old cut and stops there. Nothing above it and nothing past it.
It is Aurelian. We did not build it and we do not use it.
We keep the cairns up, though. Somebody built those, and it was not them.
Pressure, wind, cloud base, three times a day, and I send it down the wire at six.
I have sent the same reading eleven days running and it is not an instrument fault.
I asked to be recalled. They said stay and keep sending. So I am staying and sending.
Upper Caelora Station. Foundation work, and honest work: somebody has to measure it.
The cable? It goes on up the mountain to another set. Not mine, not my department.
I have never been asked what that set is for and I have stopped noticing that.
